anchor.statement: Theorem 4.6. There exist fixed h ∈ (0, 1/100), λ > 0, C > 1, and 0 < X a < X b , together with profiles E, U, Π for X ≥ 0, −1 ≤ η ≤ 1, having the following properties. The quantities F, H, V 0 , Q s , N s , p s , a, b s and T 0 are defined by Equations (4.7) to (4.11); where a > 0, t s , v s are defined in (4.20). We use A, d from (4.1). The closed annulus below means the profile rectangle [X a , X b ] × [−1, 1] in (X, η ). All assertions hold for every η ∈ [−1, 1].

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: exists_weighted_profile gives one profile (F, W, d, v) with the true cone on the active interval, weighted bounds with edge weights, and at each edge a factor with a strict, smooth direction collar; the moments, canonical pressure (4.25), analytic tube and reserved mean window are stated for the nominal witness W (or for v on the mean window) and must be transferred to v through the outside-field and history equalities of ModulatedProfileAssembly. The smooth extension of n = T0/|T0| to [Xa, Xb], one κ in (0, 2) for (4.26), the endpoint directions, h < 1/100, the reserved interval Ipos and the identification of the analytic tube with v are the reviewer's argument across modules; no declaration states the theorem for one profile.
